math.alpha.b: A constant representing after how many years the probability of a move equalizes.
math.alpha.c: A constant representing the current year.
math.alpha.t: The sum of the maximum possible values.
math.alpha.si: Year statistics for a given move.
math.alpha.abs_si: Number of years (occurrences of the move)
math.alpha.vi: Array of values calculated for each statistic
math.alpha.lambda: Scaling factor adjusted based on the maximum value.
math.alpha.l: Function determining the weight of the year
math.alpha.f: Function calculating the scaled trend value for a move
math.beta.xi: Number of games with a given move in a year
math.beta.yi: Number of points in games with a given move in a year
math.beta.ni: Number of games in a year

pol_calculator.4.3: 4.3 A norm may be awarded to a player who has played fewer games than required by Table No. 3, provided that in those games they have scored as many points as they would need to achieve over the required minimum number of games. In such a case, it is assumed that in the missing games up to the required limit, the player would have faced opponents with a rating equal to the average rating of their opponents in the tournament.
pol_calculator.4.4: 4.4 In competitions where more games have been played than the minimum required for rating evaluation, games won against players whose participation lowers the average rating may be excluded. However, the number of games submitted for rating evaluation cannot be lower than the required minimum.
pol_calculator.4.5: 4.5 If a Swiss-system tournament consists of more rounds than the required minimum, the norm may also be achieved in rounds beyond the required minimum.
pol_calculator.4.6: 4.6 In a round-robin tournament, the norm is calculated from all games played.
pol_calculator.4.7: 4.7 A norm for First Category, Candidate Master title, or Master title may be achieved in tournaments of 5–8 rounds. In such tournaments, the number of games required for achieving a norm is considered equal to the number of rounds in the tournament. When calculating norms in such tournaments, points 4.3., 4.4., and 4.5. do not apply.
pol_calculator.4.9: 4.9. A player may be awarded a III or II category based on their request, provided they have achieved an appropriate ranking result in two tournaments of 5 or 6 rounds
pol_calculator.converting_rating_explana: For foreign players who do not have a category, but have a FIDE rating, a provisional rating is assumed, which is obtained by rounding up the FIDE rating to the nearest rating point.
